correctness.rationale: Exact character sum counts admissible slopes, the two graph branches cover all nonzero quadratic norm levels bijectively, and the cyclic norm-one field-extension group acts simply transitively on each fiber. Each dilation block is the restriction of a complete character matrix to q−1 nonzero first coordinates and so forms a Parseval simplex; disjoint blocks prove global Parseval and the exact eigenvalue multiplicities. The finite checker corroborates eight cases but is not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The primary 2017 finite-wavelet paper proves a general tiling-to-frame implication and a Euclidean-rotation construction only for odd primes ≡3 mod4; its q≡1 isotropic-zero-norm obstruction does not apply to the deliberately anisotropic nonsquare norm, and its Section 5 asks for q≡1 existence and prime-power extension. The present constructed norm-transversal and all-odd-prime-power Gram classification are not consequences of its explicit construction. Other accessible adjacent texts do not cover the specific objects/parameters. Residual historical and inaccessible-full-text risks remain, so this is best-knowledge not a universal novelty proof.

value.rationale: The known Euclidean-rotation construction fails at primes q≡1 mod4 and leaves the existence of finite tight wavelet frame sets there open in the primary 2017 paper. The explicit nonsplit norm construction supplies these absent finite frames and works uniformly over nonprime odd finite fields; precise equal-norm Gram blocks and large families of graph transversals give concrete structural sampling design information.
